outcome: A preprint by Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu (arXiv:2608.27242, posted 27 Aug 2026) claims a full proof of the Arnold–Givental conjecture in complete generality, combining integral Floer theory, a reduction to Hamiltonian Floer cohomology due to Lu, and a new ℤ/2-equivariant localization argument; the paper itself records a concurrent, independent announcement of a proof by Amanda Hirschi and Noah Porcelli one day earlier (26 Aug 2026) at a conference in Augsburg. Neither has been digested by the expert community yet; only an automated preprint-review service (Pith) has produced a report, which flags an analytic step (described as a 'thin point') needing careful checking.
credited_humans: Amanda Hirschi (concurrent independent announcement, unpublished as of this record)
Noah Porcelli (concurrent independent announcement, unpublished as of this record)

disputes.summary: The Bai–Shelukhin–Wang–Xu preprint (submitted 27 Aug 2026) explicitly notes in its Remark 1.2 a concurrent, independent proof announced by Amanda Hirschi and Noah Porcelli on 26 Aug 2026 (one day earlier) at the conference 'Symplectic Topology – in honor of Kai Cieliebak' in Augsburg. No preprint from Hirschi–Porcelli could be located as of this research (checked 2026-09-22); their work was described in the announcement as 'joint work-in-progress'. Priority and completeness of each claim is unresolved.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet bundles the Arnold conjecture (fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms) and the Arnold–Givental conjecture (a Smith-inequality-type bound on Lagrangian fixed-point sets of an anti-symplectic involution) as a single entry; the triage record and my research both center on the Arnold–Givental half, since that is where the dated finding sits. As of the frozen revision (26 Jan 2024), the Arnold–Givental conjecture was open in general, proved only in a list of special cases (Givental for (CP^n, RP^n); Oh for real forms of compact Hermitian spaces; Lazzarini for the negative monotone case; Fukaya–Oh–Ohta–Ono for semi-positive (M,ω); Frauenfelder for certain symplectic reductions). On 27 August 2026, Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu posted arXiv:2608.27242 claiming a full proof in complete generality, using integral Floer theory (methods of the 1st and 4th authors), a reduction to Hamiltonian Floer cohomology due to Lu, and a new ℤ/2-equivariant localization argument. I read the abstract and the paper's own text (via the arXiv HTML rendering) directly rather than relying on the triage's unopened snippet. The paper contains no mention whatsoever of AI systems, language models, or automated theorem-proving tools in its methods or acknowledgements — the acknowledgements section credits only NSF/NSERC/FRQNT/Simons funding, so ai_role is 'none'. The paper itself discloses a genuine priority dispute: it acknowledges a concurrent, independent proof announced one day earlier (26 Aug 2026) by Amanda Hirschi and Noah Porcelli at a symplectic-topology conference in Augsburg, described as work-in-progress; I could not locate a preprint from Hirschi and Porcelli as of 22 Sep 2026, so their claim remains an announcement only. Given the preprint is barely three weeks old at the time of this research, there is no evidence of expert digestion (no blog commentary from Tao, the Matroid/symplectic-topology community blogs, or journal acceptance). The only third-party assessment found is from 'Pith' (pith.science), which is explicitly an automated/machine preprint-review service (self-described as producing 'referee-style reports' via a 'machine reviewer'), not a human expert; its report flags an analytic step as a 'thin point' needing careful checking, i.e. it has not vouched for correctness. Per §6.1, a preprint with no human expert digestion is 'claimed', not 'resolved', however clean the exposition looks; the status here is 'claimed'. The stated result answers the conjecture as expected (confirming the conjectured inequality), so resolution_direction is 'confirmed'; this is not a counterexample. I disagree with the triage record only in nuance, not substance: the triage flagged 'likely' and found the same single arXiv entry; I confirmed by reading the abstract/full text, found the priority dispute the triage missed (it had not opened the paper), and confirmed no AI involvement rather than leaving it unchecked.
competing_reading: One could argue this should be 'resolved' given the identity/reputation of the authors (Bai and Shelukhin are established Floer theorists) and the existence of a machine-generated review that did not flag outright errors, only a step needing further scrutiny. But per §6.1 a machine review is explicitly insufficient for 'resolved' status — a human expert (named, working through the argument) or journal acceptance is required, and neither exists yet for a paper posted only ~3.5 weeks before this research date.
what_would_settle_it: A human expert's public digestion of the Bai–Shelukhin–Wang–Xu argument (a seminar report, a referee report, journal acceptance, or a named symplectic geometer's blog/MathOverflow commentary working through the proof), and/or the appearance of the competing Hirschi–Porcelli preprint and any reconciliation of the two claims, would move this to 'resolved' and settle the priority dispute.

incomplete: I was unable to fetch the Pith report's full content directly (the fetch returned no page content), so I rely on a search-engine summary of it plus the Pith site's own self-description for the 'automated, not human' characterization; the exact wording of the 'thin point' remark is second-hand. I also could not locate any primary source from Hirschi or Porcelli themselves (no preprint, no personal announcement text) — the account of their conference announcement rests entirely on secondary search summaries and the rival paper's own Remark 1.2, not on a primary statement by Hirschi or Porcelli.

corrections.why: SCOPE: `claimed` counted this bullet among resolutions, but the record says the bullet bundles two conjectures, the Arnold conjecture and the Arnold-Givental conjecture, and Bai-Shelukhin-Wang-Xu claim only the second. One of the listed sub-questions settled, with the other still open, is `partial` under 6.1. The research rules fold 'how much was settled' and 'has an expert checked it' into one field, and the agent read an unreviewed result as `claimed`; that is the pattern this batch of corrections fixes. `partial` does not record review status, so the absence of expert digestion and the Hirschi-Porcelli priority question stay in `summary`.

judgement.doubts: The bullet names two conjectures (Arnold and Arnold–Givental); the preprint addresses only the Arnold–Givental one, so it is a case (F2), and the earlier human correction from claimed to partial is right. The Hirschi–Porcelli item is an oral announcement known only through the rival paper's Remark 1.2; there is no written argument, so it cannot set the status and is coded scope none. Pith's 'thin point' is automated review (F11), neither digestion nor a knock-down. No searches run: the preprint is a month old and the record was checked on 2026-09-22.
